## ✨ What's new in 0.2.9

### 🖥️ Real full screen for Remote Desktop
- An RDP session can now take over the **whole screen**, without the title bar, sidebar or status bar, instead of filling only the terminal area.
- Use **Full screen** in the status bar, or press `Ctrl+Alt+Enter` (`⌘⌥Enter` on macOS), the usual shortcut in RDP clients. Press it again to go back.
- A **connection bar** at the top (like Remote Desktop Connection's) shows the host and has **Exit full screen** and **Disconnect**. It hides itself; move the pointer to the top edge to bring it back.
- Leaving full screen with the macOS green button or `⌃⌘F` is picked up too, and a session that ends drops out of full screen on its own.
- Hosts with **Full screen** turned on in their settings now open that way in the built-in client.
- The session isn't reconnected when you switch: the picture just resizes.

### 🧹 A cleaner RDP host dialog
- With the built-in client (Settings → Terminal → **Open RDP hosts in a tab**), the host dialog shows only what it supports: resolution, full screen, resizing, clipboard and audio.
- Options only the system client has (shared folders, printers, smart cards, COM ports, microphone, cameras, USB, multiple monitors, admin session, RD Gateway) are hidden. Their saved values are kept and still apply when you choose **Open in system client**, and they all reappear if you turn the built-in client off.

### Good to know
- Need a Mac folder or a printer on the remote computer? Use **Open in system client** (Windows App). The built-in engine, [IronRDP](https://github.com/Devolutions/IronRDP), doesn't support drive or printer redirection yet.
